analysis.subject: physics
analysis.pageCoverage: Page explains how lift depends on size and pressure, how reference area is chosen for the lift equation, the definition of planform area compared to total surface area, and how flaps and slats increase wing area at low velocity during takeoff and landing.

overview.headline: Lift grows with wing area and reference area choices affect calculation

keyPoints.point: Lift depends on object size because pressure variation of air around the moving body creates aerodynamic force.
keyPoints.quote: The amount of lift generated by an object depends on the size of the object.

keyPoints.point: Lift is directly proportional to area, so doubling the area doubles the lift.
keyPoints.quote: Like the other aerodynamic force, drag, the lift is directly proportional to the area of the object.

keyPoints.point: Planform area is the wing area viewed from above along the lift direction and serves as the preferred reference area.
keyPoints.quote: The planform area is the area of the wing as viewed from above the wing, looking along the “lift” direction.

keyPoints.point: Designers increase wing area with flaps and slats during takeoff and landing at low velocity to keep lift high.
keyPoints.quote: Takeoff and landing are times of relatively low velocity, so to keep the lift high (to avoid the ground!) designers try to increase the wing area.

keyTerms.gloss: aerodynamic force created by pressure variation around a moving body
keyTerms.quote: Lift is an aerodynamic force and therefore depends on the pressure variation of the air around the body as it moves through the air.

keyTerms.gloss: force related to pressure times surface area around a body
keyTerms.quote: The total aerodynamic force is equal to the pressure times the surface area around the body.

keyTerms.gloss: flat reference area of wing as viewed from above along lift direction
keyTerms.quote: The planform area is the area of the wing as viewed from above the wing, looking along the “lift” direction.

keyTerms.gloss: experimentally determined factor from measuring lift and area to calculate lift
keyTerms.quote: Since the lift coefficient is determined experimentally,

keyTerms.gloss: wing parts sliding backwards along tracks to increase wing area
keyTerms.quote: This is done by sliding the flaps backwards along metal tracks and shifting the slats forward to increase the wing area.

keyTerms.gloss: wing parts shifting forward to increase wing area at low velocity
keyTerms.quote: This is done by sliding the flaps backwards along metal tracks and shifting the slats forward to increase the wing area.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: builds recall of proportional lift, pressure origin and reference area definitions before deeper comparison
componentPlan.focusQuote: Doubling the area doubles the lift.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: contrasts planform area and total surface area on definition and effect on coefficient to clarify reference choice
componentPlan.focusQuote: It is a flat plane, and is NOT the total surface area (top and bottom) of the entire wing, although it is almost half that number for most wings.
